title: Positive Cech column homology vanishes in an acyclic degree
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary family of opens, F an O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and I an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Fix n ≥ 0 and p > 0. Suppose for every tuple y of length n+1 the degree-p open module cohomology [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] of F on the intersection of the U(y(l)) is zero. Then the degree-p homology object of the resolution column (moduleCechDouble U I).flip.X n [def-sc-module-cech-comparison] is zero. No augmentation hypothesis or vanishing in other degrees or at other tuple lengths is needed.

source.place: Vanishing hypothesis of Tag 01ET applied to the resolution double complex of Tag 01EQ; resolution computation in Tag 01DZ; coordinate product argument expanded by E2

proof.text: By [def-sc-open-module-cohomology], open module cohomology is the right derived functor of open sections. Mathlib CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj identifies its value with the homology of sections of the prescribed resolution. Hence each tuple-intersection section complex has zero homology in degree p. Restriction of the resolution to an open is unnecessary for this direct definition.

In the column of [def-sc-module-cech-comparison], differentials are coordinatewise maps on the product over tuples. A degree-p cocycle is a tuple of coordinate cocycles; vanishing supplies preimages in degree p-1. Choose one preimage per tuple. Their tuple is a column preimage, proving exactness, hence zero homology. Restriction of scalars does not change underlying exactness. If there are no tuples the product is zero.
